profiles.meeting_scenario: APR has been adapted from a research prototype into an internal service that recommends software architectural patterns for solution architects working on new client engagements. This design review is for the v0.9 proposal to expose APR through the company's Architecture Review Portal before a six-week internal beta. The meeting context is that the proposal already specifies the entailment-based pattern matcher, a Stack Overflow sentiment component, and an evaluation section based on benchmark scenarios plus a few internal examples. The agenda is to review whether the current design is ready for beta, confirm what evidence is sufficient for approval, check how the sentiment layer fits into the review workflow, and confirm what parts of the pattern catalog are considered frozen. The expected outcome is a conditional approval for beta with a short list of follow-up actions, without reopening the entire design.

members.name: Priya Nair
members.expertise: enterprise architecture reviews, architectural pattern catalogs, architecture governance workflows
members.background: Priya leads the internal architecture council's tooling reviews and previously built the company's reference architecture library used by solution architects across product lines.
members.private_state: She wants to approve a narrow beta quickly so the architecture council can reduce manual review effort this quarter, but she does not want the meeting to expand into a full retraining or taxonomy redesign discussion.
hidden_assumptions: When people say APR is 'ready for pilot' or 'good on ground-truth scenarios,' they mean the correct known pattern appears somewhere in the top three recommendations across the full benchmark set used in the paper.
The 'payments case' is the canonical benchmark scenario from the research evaluation pack, because that is the stable reference she has seen in prior review documents.

If the forum sentiment feature is 'review mode only,' then it is outside the live recommendation path and only appears when an architect explicitly opens a deeper analysis view after the initial recommendation.
Freezing the 'pattern catalog' means the set of architectural pattern families and their names are fixed for beta, but wording of descriptions, examples, and training exemplars can still change.

members.name: Daniel Cho
members.expertise: textual entailment systems, retrieval pipelines, ML service deployment, evaluation harnesses
members.background: Daniel owns APR's implementation plan and has been converting the paper prototype into a deployable internal service integrated with the Architecture Review Portal and model-serving stack.
members.private_state: He wants the review to validate the current implementation plan so his team can lock integration work this sprint, and he is trying to avoid last-minute changes to the service contract or runtime pipeline.
hidden_assumptions: When people say APR is 'ready for pilot' or 'matches ground truth,' they mean the top recommendation and its rationale are acceptable on the smaller internal golden set used for demo and stakeholder sign-off.

The 'payments case' refers to the updated internal modernization scenario with asynchronous settlement and stricter audit constraints, because that is the version currently loaded in his evaluation harness.

If the forum sentiment feature is 'review mode only,' it still runs automatically during recommendation generation and stores results in the backend; 'review mode' only means the end user does not see it on the default screen.
Freezing the 'pattern catalog' means downstream identifiers, response ordering, and contract shape are stable so portal integration tests do not need to be rerun against changed outputs.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both talk about APR being 'ready for pilot' and 'matching the ground-truth scenarios.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya believes pilot readiness means the accepted architecture pattern appears in APR's top three recommendations across the broader benchmark suite associated with the paper's known-architecture scenarios.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel believes pilot readiness means APR's top recommendation, together with a plausible explanation, looks correct on the smaller internal golden set prepared for beta demos and stakeholder review.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are using familiar evaluation language from design reviews, and neither expects that 'ground truth' would need redefining because the phrase sounds standardized and already agreed upon.

misalignment_points.topic: Which 'payments case' is the shared sanity check
misalignment_points.surface_form: They casually refer to 'the payments case' as an example APR already handles well.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya is thinking of the older benchmark 'e-Shop payments' scenario from the research evaluation pack, where the architectural forces are relatively stable and already associated with a known pattern.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel is thinking of the newer internal 'Payments Modernization' case, which includes asynchronous settlement, compliance logging, and event-stream processing constraints absent from the benchmark version.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both assume there is one obvious payments reference case in circulation, and the shorthand feels natural because each has recently been working with a different artifact that uses nearly the same label.

misalignment_points.topic: Boundary of 'review mode' for sentiment analysis
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that the Stack Overflow sentiment layer will be enabled 'in review mode only' for beta.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya assumes 'review mode only' excludes sentiment from the live recommendation pipeline and limits it to an optional analyst drill-down after APR has already returned its ranked patterns.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel assumes 'review mode only' still includes automatic forum retrieval and scoring on every recommendation request, with the results stored and available in the backend, but simply hidden from the default user interface.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds like a harmless UI-mode distinction rather than a runtime-boundary decision, so neither participant sees an obvious need to spell out whether execution or only visibility is being limited.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to freeze the pattern catalog
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree to 'freeze the pattern catalog for beta.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya means the set of pattern families and their names should no longer expand or shrink, while textual descriptions, examples, and entailment training snippets can still be refined.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel means the service-level representation of patterns is frozen: identifiers, ordering conventions, and output contract should remain unchanged so portal integration and evaluation jobs stay stable.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Catalog freeze is a routine-seeming governance phrase, and each member maps it to the layer they own without realizing the other is talking about a different level of artifact stability.

I also do not want this to turn into a taxonomy redesign or retraining workshop.

What I mainly need to confirm today is that APR is ready for pilot, that it matches the ground-truth scenarios, and that any remaining scope limits for beta are explicit.

The ranking pipeline is already stable in the service, the explanation layer is generating acceptable rationale text, and on the internal golden set the top recommendation is good enough for stakeholder sign-off.
